summary: The Toyopet Master, introduced in January 1955, was a modernized update of the Toyota SF/RH sedan, sharing its ladder frame and leaf-sprung axles. It was sold alongside the first Toyota Crown, positioned as a frugally equipped taxi-oriented model, and shared the R-series engine with the Crown. The note also covers the Masterline commercial range (RR16 pickup, RR17 van, RR19 double pickup), which were the first car-based trucks produced in Japan and were built until a Crown-based Masterline replaced them in March 1959.
one_line: The Toyopet Master, a 1955 taxi-oriented Toyota sedan, and its Masterline commercial variants.
key_facts: The Toyopet Master was introduced in January 1955 as an update to the SF/RH model with a modernized body.
The Toyopet Master had a ladder frame with leaf sprung front and rear axles, as its predecessor did.
The Toyopet Master evolved from the Toyota SF/RH model, also known as the Super.
The Toyopet Master was sold in parallel with the first Toyota Crown.
The Master was introduced as a frugally equipped version meant for taxi usage.
The Master and Crown shared the same R-series engine.
The Master was sold at a chain of Toyota Japan dealerships called "Toyota Store", next to the more upscale Crown.
The Toyopet Master range included the Masterline RR16 pickup, the Masterline RR17 van and the Masterline RR19 double pickup.
The Masterline commercial models were introduced in November 1955, originally as a single-cab pickup and a van.
The double pickup was added in August 1956, around which time the engine was upgraded.
The Masterline commercial models replaced the SG commercial models and were the first car-based trucks to enter production in Japan.
The Masterline commercial models were carried over after the discontinuation of the Master.
The Masterline commercial models were built until a new Crown-based Masterline replaced them in March 1959 for the Toyota Store sales channel.
A smaller Coronaline version was developed to be sold through Toyopet dealers.
